solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Items logged by head of Swiss guards

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the start of Swiss is taken

parts.note: items written into a log or register are entries

explanation.surface: Records kept by the commander of the Vatican's Swiss Guard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries are soldiers posted on watch, so they are guards in the plural noun sense.

clue.text: Prison warder best get such a bottle

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison officer
top means best, as in the top student

explanation.surface: A jailer who gets the finest bottle of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwtop bottle is one closed with a threaded cap rather than a cork.

clue.text: Arrests prison warders at last

parts.note: the nick is British slang for prison

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of warders

explanation.surface: Prison officers finally make some arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick someone is British slang for arresting them, so nicks means arrests.

clue.text: A square meal in Italy?

parts.note: a square meal usually means a filling one, but here it is literally an Italian dish of square pasta parcels

explanation.surface: Wondering what counts as a hearty dinner in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian dish consists of small square pasta pockets with a filling, literally square food.

clue.text: Land before one is accepted

indicators.note: is accepted means one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Arriving on land before someone is admitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, a country or land.

clue.text: Sort of kingdom where the soul has left

parts.note: anima is the Latin word for the soul, used in Jungian psychology for the inner self

explanation.surface: A realm where the spirit has departed, a gloomy philosophical musing.
explanation.definitionFit: Biology classifies life into kingdoms, and the animal kingdom is one of them.

clue.text: Wanting to be born, died with bad flu

parts.note: née means born, used before a woman's maiden name
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of flu are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A gloomy wish to have been born only to die from a nasty bout of influenza.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful means needed or required; as a noun-like adjective it fits wanting in the sense of lacking or needing.

clue.text: A poor actor raised on Irish jigs by a teacher from India

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, so the actor word is turned around

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting actor

indicators.note: jigs suggests dancing about, so the letters of Irish are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mediocre actor performs Irish dances alongside an Indian guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns HAM to MAH; 'jigs' rearranges IRISH to RISHI.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharishi is a Hindu sage or spiritual teacher, a title from India.

clue.text: Pay attention to legal right crossing the road

indicators.note: crossing means the legal right straddles the road, holding it inside

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to keep another's property until a debt is paid
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: Heed your legal right of way when crossing the street.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen is to pay attention to sounds or advice.

clue.text: Doubly insured, but got better!

definitions.meaning: covered means insured, and covered again is insured a second time
... from an illness, became healthy again

explanation.surface: A patient with two insurance policies who then made a full recovery anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as RE-COVERED: covered again, so insured twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain health, so the past tense means got better; split, it means covered once more.

clue.text: Meaning home guard started wandering

parts.note: the drift of an argument is its gist or meaning
in means at home

indicators.note: started signals the starting letter of guard

explanation.surface: The Home Guard's attention began to wander.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Guard was Britain's Second World War volunteer defence force, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Drifting means moving aimlessly, wandering without direction.

clue.text: Philosophy that's central to budget hospitals

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of the run budget hospitals, straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A guiding principle at the heart of a hospital budget.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of guiding beliefs, a philosophy of a group.

clue.text: The advisability of holding one's party in wardroom that's empty

indicators.note: holding means the emptied word clasps the other letters inside it
an empty word has lost its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: one's read as one is, giving I (one) plus S, or simply IS
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Debating whether it is wise to throw a party in the deserted officers' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' stands for 'one is', so it gives IS. A wardroom is the officers' mess on a warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom here is soundness of a course of action, as in the wisdom of doing something, a synonym of advisability.

clue.text: Service's push following broadcast

definitions.note: read as service is, the definition being the noun service, an armed force

indicators.note: following means the push comes after the broadcast in the answer

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
to force is to push

explanation.surface: A military service makes a promotional push after a television broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The air force is one of the armed services, alongside the army and navy.

clue.text: Sailor given cards repeatedly

parts.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards
a hand is the set of cards dealt to one player

explanation.surface: A seaman dealt cards over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' tells you to use 'cards' twice, in two different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckhand is a member of a ship's crew who works on deck, a sailor.

clue.text: A love's wildest fancy stories from the past

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, so the letters are freely reimagined in a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, the apostrophe ignored, make the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone's most extravagant romantic fantasy, an imagined tale of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' signals that the thirteen letters of A LOVES WILDEST are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Old wives' tales are traditional superstitions and beliefs handed down, stories from times gone by.

clue.text: Particularly high wind?

parts.note: particularly is read as full of particles, a strong wind laden with fine grit

explanation.surface: Asking whether the wind is especially strong today.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust storm is a strong wind carrying clouds of dust particles across dry land.

clue.text: Operator accepts source of tuna fish

indicators.note: accepts means the operator takes the letter inside

parts.note: a surgeon operates on patients

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A machine operator takes delivery of tuna for the fish counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sturgeon is a large fish, the source of caviar.

clue.text: Impasse reached after running through detail

parts.note: to stick someone is to run them through with a blade
a point is a particular item or detail in an argument

explanation.surface: A negotiation reaches deadlock after going through the fine print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reached after' joins the definition to the wordplay; 'running through' looks like reading a document but means stabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sticking point is an issue on which agreement cannot be reached, so a deadlock or impasse.

clue.text: Attacks suffered by popular routes

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
roads are routes for travel

explanation.surface: Raids suffered along well-used routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are hostile raids or incursions into territory, so attacks.

clue.text: Flag waver requires a light touch in front of public violence

indicators.note: in front of places the light touch before the violence in the answer

parts.note: a pat is a light touch with the hand
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A demonstrator waving a flag needs a gentle hand before the crowd turns violent.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot loves their country and might literally wave its flag.

clue.text: Family help couple to chase gold

indicators.note: to chase is to come after, so the couple follows the gold in the answer

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A couple hired to help a family are out for money.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreign person who helps a host family with childcare and housework.

clue.text: Displayed route maps without old contraflow

indicators.note: displayed is read as splayed out or set out anew, so the letters are rearranged
without means the letter for old is removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Road maps showing the routes of a traffic contraflow.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O from ROUTEMAPS to leave RUTEMAPS, which 'Displayed' rearranges. A contraflow is a British roadworks system of traffic running against its normal direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means moving against the current, so a flow in the contrary direction.

clue.text: Reversing places with soldiers in a daze

indicators.note: reversing turns the word for places back to front

parts.note: to put is to place, so puts means places
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers who keep swapping positions end up dazed and confused.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a state of near-unconsciousness, a dazed condition.

clue.text: Mostly idle during public address from square

indicators.note: during means the shortened word sits inside the public address

parts.note: PA is the abbreviation for public address, as in a PA system

indicators.note: mostly means the word for idle loses its final letter

parts.note: lazy means idle

explanation.surface: A lazy announcement made over loudspeakers in a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the final letter of the synonym for idle before it goes inside; PA as public address is the loudspeaker system heard in a square.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square in a town.

clue.text: Part of church where service initially is covered by primate

indicators.note: is covered by means the service letter is enclosed by the primate

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of service

explanation.surface: In one part of the church, the service is led by an archbishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primate' suggests a senior archbishop, fitting the church setting, but here it is an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: A foreign capital and its smell?

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name for Rome, a capital city spelt the foreign way

explanation.surface: Asking whether a foreign capital city has its own distinctive odour.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a distinctive, usually pleasant, smell.

clue.text: Bridge match?

definitions.meaning: a form of the card game in which every table plays the same deals
a match is an exact copy of something

explanation.surface: A question about a bridge tournament fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: In the competitive form of bridge named this way, the same hands are replayed at every table to cancel out luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A match in the sense of an identical counterpart is a copy, and the bridge variant takes the same name.

clue.text: Delinquent young lady chasing soldiers

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the young lady follows the soldiers in the answer

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
miss is a title for a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A wayward girl running after soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent in one's duty, an adjective sense close to delinquent.

clue.text: Hold back and relax before shower

indicators.note: before means the word for relax precedes the shower in the answer

parts.note: to rest is to relax
a shower is a short fall of rain

explanation.surface: Advice to stay put and unwind before the rain arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to check or keep under control, to hold back.
